doc.title: RegExp Class
doc.para: Regular Expression Patterns Regular expression patterns can be specified enclosed between / and /. Please refer to .
compile The compile method sets a new regular expression pattern for the regular expression object. The arguments are identical to those specified for the RegExp class constructor.

test The test method returns whether the string specified in the argument matches the pattern.
Syntax: test(<string>)
Returns true if it matches the pattern, and false if it does not. This method updates the values of each property of this object.

exec The exec method performs regular expression pattern matching on the string specified in the argument and returns an array containing the match results.
Syntax: exec(<string>)
If it does not match the pattern, the number of elements in the array will be 0. If it matches, element 0 (the first element) contains the entire matched portion, and subsequent elements contain each captured group (the parts specified by ( ) in the regular expression pattern). This method updates the values of each property of this object.

match The match method is identical to the exec method, except that it does not update the property values of this object.
Syntax: match(<string>)

replace The replace method performs string replacement and returns the string after replacement.
Syntax: replace(<target string>, <replacement string>)
It performs matching on the target string, replaces the matched portion with the replacement string, and returns the string after replacement. If a function is passed instead of a string as the replacement string, that function will be called to perform the replacement. The function takes one argument, which is an array object representing the matched portion in the target string (see the exec method for details on this array). The matched portion in the target string is replaced with the string returned by the function. This method ignores the start property.

split The split method splits a string.
Syntax: split(<target string>, <(reserved)>, <ignore empty elements=false>)
Returns an array object storing the results of splitting the string. Please also refer to the split method in .

matches The matches property is a read-only property representing an array containing each matched portion. If it does not match the pattern, the number of elements in the array will be 0. If it matches, element 0 (the first element) contains the entire matched portion, and subsequent elements contain each captured group (the parts specified by ( ) in the regular expression pattern).
start A property representing the search start position in the string. A value can also be set.
index A read-only property representing the position of the first character in the matched portion. 0 represents the beginning, so if it is the first character of the target string, it will be 0.
lastIndex A read-only property representing the position of the character following the last character of the matched portion. 0 represents the beginning.
input A read-only property representing the target string to be matched.
leftContext A read-only property representing the portion of the target string to the left of the matched part.
rightContext A read-only property representing the portion of the target string to the right of the matched part.
lastMatch Represents the matched string. Same as matches[0].
lastParen Returns the last captured part among each matched portion. Same as matches[matches.count-1].
